name: NEAR Shoemaker at Eros
keyDiscovery: The first spacecraft to orbit and touch down on an asteroid in human history. Proved that 433 Eros is a pristine, undifferentiated rubble-pile asteroid from the dawn of our solar system without a global magnetic field.
missionLegacy: Pioneered low-gravity proximity operations around irregularly shaped minor bodies, laying the direct engineering foundation for OSIRIS-REx, Hayabusa, and DART planetary defense missions.
funFact: NEAR was never designed to land! It had no landing gear or shock absorbers. Engineers gently tapped the thrusters to slow its descent to just 1.7 meters per second — slower than human walking speed — and it survived the impact, transmitting signals from the asteroid surface for two full weeks!
heritageNote: NEAR Shoemaker remains intact on the boulder-strewn surface of Asteroid 433 Eros, serving as humanity's very first permanent monument on a near-Earth asteroid.

objects.name: NEAR Shoemaker Spacecraft
objects.description: Octagonal spacecraft bus measuring 1.5 x 1.7 meters with four gallium arsenide solar panels and a 1.5-meter high-gain antenna dish. Rested upright on Eros after an improvised gentle landing on February 12, 2001.
objects.whySent: To conduct the first dedicated long-term orbital study of a near-Earth asteroid, measuring its physical dimensions, mass distribution, mineralogy, and internal structure.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Confirmed that Eros is a consolidated chunk of primitive ordinary chondrite material with a density of 2.67 g/cm³, nearly identical to Earth's continental crust.
objects.ongoingScience: Historical orbital tracking data from NEAR remains the primary benchmark for designing planetary defense kinetic impactors and asteroid deflection models.
objects.firstPerson: History books called it impossible, but I pulled it off! I am NEAR Shoemaker. I was built as an orbiter with zero landing legs. But after circling this 33-kilometer potato-shaped asteroid for a year, engineers decided: 'Why not touch down?' We gently kissed the boulders at 4 miles per hour. Miraculously, my antennas kept transmitting data right from the rock! I am humanity's first footprint on an asteroid!

objects.name: XGRS Gamma-Ray Spectrometer
objects.description: Combined X-ray and Gamma-Ray Spectrometer mounted to detect characteristic fluorescent X-rays (magnesium, aluminum, silicon) and gamma-ray lines (iron, potassium, thorium) from Eros's surface.
objects.whySent: To determine the elemental bulk composition of Eros and resolve whether near-Earth asteroids are primitive chondrites or melted differentiated cores.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Proved Eros never underwent melting or differentiation, meaning its minerals have remained virtually unchanged since condensing from the solar nebula 4.56 billion years ago.
objects.ongoingScience: Spectroscopic calibration techniques refined on NEAR form the foundation for modern asteroid mining and resource prospecting algorithms.
objects.firstPerson: I read asteroid atomic barcodes! I am XGRS. From just 4 inches above the dust after touchdown, I bathed the regolith in my detectors and counted magnesium and silicon atoms. I proved Eros is a pristine cosmic time capsule that never got baked or melted when our solar system was born.

objects.name: Gallium Arsenide Solar Arrays
objects.description: Four rigid solar array wings spanning 5.6 meters total, utilizing high-efficiency GaAs cells generating 1,800 watts at 1 AU from the Sun.
objects.source: JHU APL Technical Digest / Jenkins et al.
objects.whySent: To supply electrical power across wildly fluctuating solar distances as Eros loops from 1.13 to 1.78 astronomical units away from the Sun.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Demonstrated that gallium arsenide photovoltaic cells could survive severe deep-space radiation belts and micrometeroid bombardment without catastrophic voltage loss.
objects.ongoingScience: Accelerated commercial adoption of GaAs multi-junction solar cells for high-radiation deep space probes.
objects.firstPerson: Four wings of pure solar power! Even when Eros tumbled wildly through space casting crazy shadows, my gallium arsenide cells soaked up every beam of sunlight to keep the radio purring. When we landed, two of my wings rested directly on the cold asteroid dirt!

objects.name: Eros Ponded Regolith Feature
objects.description: A flat, crater-free 'pond' of ultra-fine dust accumulated in low gravitational depressions on Eros, created by electrostatic levitation and acoustic seismic shaking.
objects.source: Icarus (Robinson et al. 2002) / NEAR MSI Camera
objects.whySent: To investigate the strange microgravity dust transport mechanisms unique to small airless planetary bodies.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Discovered that micrometeorite impacts trigger global seismic vibrations that cause fine electrostatic dust to flow like fluid and settle into completely flat dust ponds.
objects.ongoingScience: Crucial for planning future robotic and human surface operations on Phobos, Deimos, and hazardous near-Earth asteroids.
objects.firstPerson: I look like a serene zen sand garden on an alien rock! I am an Eros dust pond. In microgravity where gravity is 1,000 times weaker than Earth, solar radiation charges tiny dust grains and makes them float across the surface until they settle into glass-smooth lakes. Walk gently, space explorer!
